description: Department: Building Fabric - Delivery Employment Type: Full Time Location: South West Reporting To: Matt Ford Description Harmony is on a mission to be the best life safety partner to work with and for. Rated an ‘Outstanding Employer’ by Best Companies in 2025, we are only getting bigger and stronger — and we’re looking for A-players to help us get there. We are passionate about making a difference and obsessed with quality. Our goal is to build a world where every resident can sleep safely at night, knowing their home is 100% safe. This is a field-based role covering sites across the country. If you are detail-oriented, technically credible, and want to be part of a business that is genuinely committed to saving lives — read on. Clear and professional communicator — comfortable engaging with building managers, residents, and client representatives on site. Able to manage your own workload and travel schedule independently. Nice to Have Experience working across social housing, residential high-rise, or large commercial portfolios. Knowledge of fire door hardware, ironmongery, and certification requirements. Background in passive fire protection or wider fire safety. Job Benefits This is a chance to build your career at one of the UK’s fastest-growing fire safety specialists — carrying out meaningful inspection work that directly contributes to the safety of residents in buildings across the country. At Harmony, we ask a lot — and we give a lot back. The hours are real, the standards are high and the work is demanding, but for those who show up, deliver and go the extra mile, the rewards follow. title: Terms of Reference Yegna Gize Program: Data Collectors
description: Who We Are Girl Effect is an international non-profit dedicated to addressing challenges faced by adolescent girls and youth in Ethiopia. Operating in the country since 2013, the organization leverages Social and Behavior Change Communication (SBCC) strategies, combining media and on-the-ground interventions to tackle various societal issues and empower young people. Girl Effect Ethiopia created the youth brand Yegna in 2014 since then has reached over 10 million people through multiple products, outreach programs, girl networks, and research pieces done all for the betterment of adolescent lives. We create safe spaces for girls, sharing facts and answering questions about health, nutrition, education, relationships, etc. And we use innovative technology so we can reach girls at scale. We arm girls with the skills to negotiate and redefine what they are told is possible, so every girl can choose to be in control of her body, her health, her learning and her livelihood. When a girl unlocks her power to make different choices that change her life, it inspires others to do so too. She starts a ripple effect that impacts her family, community, and country. That’s the Girl Effect. 1. Background Girl Effect aims to address the challenges faced by young people in accessing sustainable livelihoods and entrepreneurial opportunities across Ethiopia. In many regions, youth face high unemployment rates, limited access to resources, and a lack of knowledge about viable business opportunities. Girl Effect seeks to empower young people by building their skills, fostering entrepreneurship, and supporting the establishment of profitable businesses. The Yegna Gize program is a three-year initiative (Dec 2024–Dec 2027) funded to empower Ethiopian youth by fostering positive mindsets, transforming community attitudes, and advancing gender inclusivity in leadership and economic participation. 2. Objective Girl Effect is updating its roster of freelance data collectors and would like to request CVs from interested data collectors. The main objective of the data collection or assessment is to quantify and assess mindset shifts and knowledge gain through the program interventions, and to capture regional-level challenges and learnings for program management and adaptations. 3. Scope of Work The Data Collectors will be responsible for gathering high-quality data from youth beneficiaries residing in: Amhara Region: ALBUKO, DESSIE, DESSIE ZURIYA, HAYKE, KALU, KOMBOLCHA, KUTABER, TEHULEDERE Central Ethiopia Region: HOSSANA, LEMO, SHAGSHOGO, SORO, ATOTA ULA, WERA, WERADEJO, ANGACHA, DAMBOYA, TEMBARO Oromia Region: ASELLA, BEKOJI, AD'A (BISHOFTU), ADAMA, ADAMI TULU, ARSI NEGELLE, BATU, DODOLA, SHASHEME, WONDO Sidama Region: ALETA CHUKO, ALETA WENDO, DALE, DARA, DERARA, HAWASSA, HAWASSA ZURIYA, SHEBE DINO, TULA, WONDOGENET South Ethiopia Region: ABELA ABAYA, BODITI, BOLOSO SORE, DAMOT PULASA, DAMOT WOIDE, GESUBA, HUMBO, OFA, SODO, SODO ZURIYA Tigray Region: SHIRE, ENDERTA, MEKELLE, MEKELLE ZURIYA, MAICHEW, MOHONI, ABIADI, ADAWA, AXUM, TAHTAY MAYCHEW Key responsibilities include: Administering digital or paper-based pre-training and post-training surveys. Conducting Focus Group Discussions (FGDs) or Key Informant Interviews (KIIs) if required. Ensuring accurate data entry and real-time synchronization with the central database. Verifying participant demographic consistency and capturing their responses accordingly. Duration: August 2026 – December 2027 based on call Locations: Amhara, Tigray, Oromia, Sidama, South Ethiopia and Central Ethiopia Engagement: Data collectors will be contacted and engaged based on the need for data collection at the time. Engagements will be assigned on an as-needed basis, depending on the scope, location, and timing of each specific assessment 3.1 Methods To ensure high-quality data and impactful of the Yegna Gize Program, the following Mixed-Methods Approach is used: Quantitative Administered via mobile devices (KoboToolbox/ODK) to all sampled participants to measure knowledge gain in growth mindset,entrepreneurship and other behavioural changes. Real-time cross-referencing of participant information against the provided participant list to ensure 80% young women and 5% vulnerable group representation. Qualitative Conducting longitudinal study to gather the impact of the programs and its learning Conducting FGD and KII for deep dive understanding of the program impacts and qualities Sample size The sample size will be determined based on program activities and available data during the interventions with a confidence level for a 95% margin of errors. Quality Assurance The data collector must adhere to guidance provided by MEL and program leads for gathering information with pre and post activity interventions. This will help to capture changes due to the program interventions across the journey the participants passed through. Requirements and Experience Bachelor’s degree in Statistics,Information management

title: Team Lead (Stabilisation and Peacebuilding)
description: Chemonics seeks a Team Leader for an anticipated multi-year programme supporting civilian dialogue, locally led peacebuilding, and the strengthening of Sudanese civil society organisations. The multi-year programme will look to support civilian dialogue and locally led peacebuilding in Sudan. The component for which Chemonics is bidding will operate as a fund management platform: making and managing grants to Sudanese civil society, community and diaspora organisations, and providing the assurance, accompaniment and learning functions that allow those organisations to work safely and effectively. The programme is not a service delivery or humanitarian programme. The programme will be delivered by a consortium of international and Sudanese partners, working across areas under different authorities and in exile. It will operate a deliberately light international platform in order to maximise the proportion of funding reaching Sudanese organisations, and will take an adaptive, politically informed approach in a volatile and rapidly changing operating environment. Role Summary The Team Leader is the most senior representative of the programme and is accountable to the Chemonics Programme Director for the overall success of programme delivery. They own the programme strategy, lead the consortium, manage senior stakeholder relationships, and ensure that the fund remains politically informed, conflict sensitive, and able to adapt as the operating context evolves. The Team Leader will be based in Addis Ababa, with regular rotation to Port Sudan and travel elsewhere in Sudan and the region as security conditions permit. Key Responsibilities Stakeholder and Donor Leadership Serve as the primary interface with programme stakeholders and funding partners, and act as the senior point of contact for any additional financing partners should the programme become a multi-donor initiative. Represent the programme to diplomatic missions, regional actors, and other relevant stakeholders, ensuring that programme outputs are responsive to broader engagement and policy priorities related to Sudan. Ensure coherence and division of labour with adjacent donor and multilateral programming in Sudan, avoiding duplication and unintended competition for the same local networks. Represent the programme in relevant coordination and learning forums with donors, the United Nations, and international and Sudanese peacebuilding actors. Strategy, Adaptation, and Thinking and Working Politically Own and periodically revise the programme strategy, theory of change, and prioritisation framework, ensuring resources are targeted strategically rather than spread evenly across themes and geographies. Lead a thinking and working politically approach across the programme, ensuring funding decisions reflect the political economy and conflict dynamics of the areas in which the programme operates. Convene consortium partners around scheduled reprogramming points and lead the implementation of agreed triggers to pause, pivot, or scale activities in response to changing circumstances. Ensure the programme maintains a credible, non-aligned position across areas under different authorities and is not perceived as aligned with any party to the conflict. Consortium Leadership Lead the consortium as a single, coherent delivery team under one management structure, with clear roles, decision-making authority, and escalation processes. Manage and periodically review partner roles, functions, and capacity, leading the onboarding and offboarding of partners as programme needs evolve. Represent the consortium to Chemonics leadership and external stakeholders and resolve disputes between partners when required. Promote an equitable partnership approach with Sudanese organisations rather than a subcontracting relationship and guard against the concentration of funding among a small number of well-connected organisations.
